title: 280. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Graphing Tangent and Its Asymptotes
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Vertical Asymptotes of the Tangent Parent Graph
questions.learningObjective: Identify the vertical asymptotes of \(y=\tan x\).
questions.question: Where does the graph of \(y=\tan x\) have vertical asymptotes?
questions.explanation: The tangent function is undefined where \(\cos x=0\). The cosine function equals zero at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\) for integers \(k\). Therefore the graph of \(y=\tan x\) has vertical asymptotes at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Recall where the cosine function equals zero.

questions.concept: Period of the Tangent Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the period of the parent tangent function \(y=\tan x\)?
questions.explanation: The tangent function repeats its values every \(\pi\) units. Unlike sine and cosine, its period is \(\pi\), not \(2\pi\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the repeating interval of the tangent graph with that of sine and cosine.

questions.concept: Domain of the Tangent Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the domain of \(y=\tan x\)?

options.label: B
options.text: All real numbers except \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\), where \(k\) is an integer

questions.explanation: The tangent function is undefined wherever \(\cos x=0\). This occurs at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\). Therefore the domain is all real numbers except these values, so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Exclude the values where the denominator of \(\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) is zero.

questions.concept: X-Intercepts of the Tangent Parent Graph
questions.question: Where does the graph of \(y=\tan x\) cross the \(x\)-axis?
questions.explanation: The \(x\)-intercepts occur where \(\tan x=0\). Since \(\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), this happens where \(\sin x=0\), which is \(x=k\pi\) for integers \(k\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Find where the sine function equals zero.

questions.concept: Range of the Tangent Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the range of \(y=\tan x\)?
questions.explanation: Between consecutive vertical asymptotes, the tangent function increases from \(-\infty\) to \({+\infty}\), so it takes every real value. Therefore the range is all real numbers, so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Observe how the tangent graph behaves as it approaches each vertical asymptote.

questions.concept: Vertical Asymptotes of a Horizontally Shifted Tangent Graph
questions.question: Where does the graph of \(y=\tan\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) have vertical asymptotes?
questions.explanation:
Set the argument equal to the asymptote location of the parent tangent function, then solve for \(x\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x-\frac{\pi}{4} &= \frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\\
x &= \frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\\
&= \frac{3\pi}{4}+k\pi
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Set the argument of the tangent function equal to \(\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\) and solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Monotonicity of the Tangent Parent Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine the behavior of \(y=\tan x\) between consecutive vertical asymptotes.
questions.question: On each interval between consecutive vertical asymptotes, how does the graph of \(y=\tan x\) behave?
questions.explanation: On each interval \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi,\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\right)\), the tangent function increases from \(-\infty\) to \({+\infty}\). Therefore the graph is increasing on each such interval, so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Consider how the tangent values change as \(x\) moves from left to right between two asymptotes.

questions.concept: Y-Intercept of the Tangent Parent Graph
questions.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\tan x\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x=0\) into \(y=\tan x\): \(y=\tan 0=0\). Therefore the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,0)\), so option B is correct.

questions.concept: Symmetry of the Tangent Parent Graph
questions.question: The graph of \(y=\tan x\) has which type of symmetry?
questions.explanation: The tangent function satisfies \(\tan(-x)=-\tan x\), so it is an odd function. Therefore its graph is symmetric about the origin, so option A is correct.
